description: A 3D-printing tool that turns type and SVG drawings into a matched pair of male and female embossing dies, using HarfBuzz and Clipper, that reads every font on the computer and exports print-ready STL files.

prompts.text:
I want to create a web app that can automatically generate STL files for embossing dies that I plan to 3d print. Right now, I'm making them manually in fusion and it's taking a long time (included is an image of a male die where I've finished the "h" in "Zach". Here's how I've been making the embossing dies:

* create a rectangular sketch and add text inside

* explode and extrude the text and base of the male die
* duplicate the die and offset the faces on the sides of the extruded letterforms a bit in order to create the negative for the female die (slightly looser than the male to provide wiggle room for the embossing material
* for the male die, first fillet the vertical sharp edges at the corners of text, then fillet the top edges of the text as well as the edges where the text meets the baseplate
* for the female die, fillet the top face at the edges where it meets the text, and fillet the bottom crevices in the text recesses


I want the web app to work as follows:

* I can type text in any font that I upload (there should also already be default web fonts installed like helvetica, arial, times new roman, etc)
* I can also add any svgs that I want to upload

*  I can then adjust the padding (ie the negative space that the "plate" portion of the dies beyond the horizontal and vertical edges of the text/svgs), which should adapt automatically to go around the objects on the canvas
* I can then specify the extrusion distance for the plates and text, as well as the amount I want to offset the female die
* The fillets should be applied automatically to first round out any sharp edges in the text's letterforms and then have the maximum fillet so that fillets at the top and bottom of the extrusions/recesses meet perfectly and the two dies can slide together smoothly.
* I should be able to control the fillet of the edges of the die plates as well (both filleting the four corners as well as the top edge of the plates


As I'm doing this, in the center of the canvas, I should be able to see the male and female dies side by side (text side up on both) being generated as I text and input extrusion/offset values , as well as view the canvas where I'm building my design for the dies in 2d/flat/illustrator-style (include a toggle to switch between 2d (design) and 3d (preview) modes.

Ctrl z to undo /+shift to redo, text size measured in mm height, padding measured in mm, anchor points to resize text and svg objects on the 2d canvas, minimal/clear/simple coloring/lighting on the 3d preview. I should be able to export both dies at once side by side and specify the distance between the two. I should be able to export as svg directly to downloads.
